From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs: next steps for execution

Ben / Emma —

Thanks — taking point on the legal redline. High-level observations after a first pass:
- Processor roles: ProspectHealth's redline wants a stronger statement that Redwood is strictly a processor and that any subprocessor engagement requires prior written notice plus a mechanism for objection. We can accept notice + objection for named subprocessor classes, but we will need to keep some operational flexibility (e.g., infra scaling, ephemeral cache providers). Suggested compromise: notice + 10 business day cure/objection window for new named subprocessors, and a categorical list for routine infra services (CDN, monitoring, logging) that are pre-authorized.
- KMS & Key control: We can offer a customer-managed envelope key (CMEK) option for Dedicated/Private deployments and a bring-your-own-key path for on-prem/VPC. For Hosted EU workloads, full customer-controlled root key via our KMS integration is possible with a standard lead time. We cannot promise HSM on short notice for Hosted without a dedicated onboarding timeline and a technical workback.
- Transfer-impact addendum / SCCs: ProspectHealth has requested explicit SIAs around onward transfers. We will propose a short addendum that references the standard EU SCCs + a table of subprocessor flows; however, we cannot accept language that broadens our liability beyond the SCCs.

Action items I'll deliver Monday EOD: 1) one-page redline summary; 2) proposed transfer-impact addendum wording (two short paragraphs + table stub); 3) a redline-friendly comment for the order form if a pricing or SLA annotation becomes necessary.

A couple of quick questions for ProspectHealth to speed signoff:
- Are there any named subprocessors you want pre-authorized (e.g., specific cloud partner or backup vendor)?
- If you need HSM-backed CMEK for Hosted, is the procurement team prepared for a 6–8 week onboarding?
